v1.feedback: The spring-coil intermediate is a genuine surprise mechanic — particles spiraling into a helix mid-morph before uncoiling into the target is exactly the kind of swerve the brief asked for, and both endpoint forms (L-system cypress, tiered art-deco tower) are structurally legit with recognizable silhouettes. Tighten the coil radius and slow the mid-transition dwell so the helix reads as a deliberate third form rather than a blur between states; right now the coil phase risks looking like scrambled noise at speed. Consider pulling the camera closer (camera.position.set(10, 7, 16)) and narrowing FOV to 32 so the 70k particles fill more frame — the current framing leaves generous empty canvas around both poses.

v2.feedback: Both endpoint forms — L-system cypress and tiered art-deco tower — are well-constructed with clear silhouettes and good particle density, and the warm-to-cool palette crossfade is restrained. But 'spring-uncoil' barely shows up: the morph is a standard staggered lerp, not an actual coiled-to-straight path. Particles should trace helical arcs during transition (e.g. cubic Bezier with a rotational component keyed to morph progress) so you literally see springs uncoiling between the two poses. The idea needs to live in the transition geometry, not just the label.
